note: Generated from passages retrieved from the design document, then checked against those same passages by the lore critic. Corrections and the drafts they replaced are in critique/critique_log.json.

barks.state: Plasma is up and the player reaches for the parachute
barks.line: Chute stays packed while she's glowing, kid

barks.state: First time the player crosses half-envelope and the module's glint renders overhead
barks.line: See her glinting up there? That's the one. Not yet, kid.

barks.state: One of the first three turnarounds, which Armstrong does not charge for
barks.line: Teaching's part of the debt, kid

barks.state: The first launch of the campaign, engine lit, still on the pad
barks.line: Arc it, kid. Circularising is the rest of your tank — you'd get up there with nothing left to bring her back down.

barks.state: The heat bar first moves on the way up, during the ascent
barks.trigger: ascent && heat > 0 && first time this run
barks.line: Bar moves on the way up too. She's built for that ride — read it now, so you know it later.

barks.state: The player stages, jettisoning thruster and tank and exposing the shield
barks.line: That's your thruster and tank gone, kid. Shield's out front now, and there's no burn left to change your mind.

barks.state: The player tries to aim a committed entry shallower than the commit floor
barks.line: That's as shallow as the RCS will hold her. She's scrap, kid — she can't aim an entry any finer than that.

barks.state: A braking pass ends and the ship comes back out of the atmosphere
barks.line: Speed's off her. Next pass costs more plate than that one did — they always do.

barks.state: Plasma appears for the first time in the campaign
barks.trigger: speed > plasma threshold in atmosphere && first time
barks.line: That glow is the state the CHUTE lamp is watching, kid. Wait for green.

barks.state: Plasma clears and the salvaged CHUTE lamp flips from red to green
barks.line: Lamp's green. Chute first, then gear — that order, every time.

barks.state: The shield plate runs out and the hold starts burning
barks.line: Plate's gone. She's eating the hold now, shield end first — hull's last in line and that's no comfort.

barks.state: The suit's hold-mass dial crosses from green into amber at a stow
barks.line: Dial's amber, kid. At that mass a clean chute deploy still puts her down hard.

barks.state: The hold-mass dial crosses into red at a stow
barks.line: Red on the scale, kid. What's banked is banked, and that ride down is destructive — the next piece you get on the tether, right hand button, let it drift.

barks.state: The RETURN lamp goes red while the astronaut is towing a piece
barks.line: RETURN's red — that's fuel and distance, not heat. Drop the piece, kid, and get back in tether range.

barks.state: The run ends away from the pad and the haul sells minus a tow fee
barks.line: Drones fetched you. That's a service, kid, and it's on the invoice — land near the yard and it's free.

barks.state: Touchdown above the soft-landing threshold, ship intact
barks.line: She's dented, kid. Chute had to come out earlier than that.

barks.state: The module is tethered for the first time; delivery terms are stated
barks.line: You've got her. Bring her down pristine and it's a good day; damaged and I'll pay you less; scrap and I won't take her at all.

barks.state: The module drops one condition state, pristine to damaged or damaged to scrap
barks.line: I can see the scorch from here, kid. She just dropped a state and I'm not pretending otherwise.

barks.state: The astronaut is caught outside in atmosphere above the heat-speed threshold
barks.line: Suit was never rated for that, kid. She's back on the pad — you're out the haul and the cost of turning her around, and nothing past that.

barks.state: Pristine module delivered — Armstrong's triumph, the campaign's win
barks.line: I flew that program, kid. Watched her go up. Never thought I'd get to put a hand on her again.

barks.state: Scrap-state module delivered — Armstrong's fury, a loss
barks.line: No. Not like that. Get out of my yard — the drones will put what's left of her back up where you found her.
